{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABiIYagw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhLgFUo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 146, "title": "Separate player controls from gameplay, resume after tab visibility changes, and limit fullscreen to gameplay", "body": "## Problem

Three related UI/UX problems remain after the recent mobile controller redesign (#142 / #143):

1. **Accidental Pause/Reset on phones.** The player toolbar is below or near the virtual X/Y keypads, A/B and Start. A finger slipping off a game button can activate a player-management control. Accidentally restarting a game is especially disruptive because in-game progress since the last save may be lost.
2. **Tab visibility interrupts play unnecessarily.** Hiding the tab correctly pauses emulation, but returning to it currently requires a manual Resume even when the user never asked to pause.
3. **Fullscreen includes unrelated UI.** The current implementation requests fullscreen on the entire `#player`, including the header, toolbar, cartridge picker entry point and console selector. Fullscreen should focus on gameplay, not the whole application.

The intended solution is better spatial separation, not extra confirmation steps or complicated menus. Use the sibling [snes-rust player](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/) as a reference for the Reset label and gameplay-only fullscreen structure, while preserving WonderSwan's distinct controller geometry and visibility-pause policy.

## Expected outcome

- On a phone, the regular player-management toolbar is **above the game area**, separated from the virtual controller. Pause and Reset remain directly accessible but are not adjacent to the X/Y keypads, A/B or Start.
- Rename the user-facing **Restart** control and corresponding help/recovery text to **Reset**, consistent with snes-rust and common console terminology. Reset retains the existing deliberate reset/reboot behavior. **Do not add a confirmation dialog, long-press requirement, double-tap requirement, or extra menu.** A single intentional activation resets the game.
- When a running game is automatically suspended because the document becomes hidden, resume it automatically when the document becomes visible again, provided no other condition blocks playback. A deliberately paused game stays paused; an unloaded, loading, faulted or modal-blocked game must not be started by an inappropriate visibility callback.
- Fullscreen targets the gameplay presentation container (`#game` or a minimal equivalent), not `#player` or the page. Only the game picture, appropriate virtual game controls, and a discreet fullscreen-exit control on touch devices are visible. Desktop keyboard/mouse users can exit with Escape/native browser controls. No header, Pause/Reset, cartridge/console controls, regular toolbar or unrelated settings in fullscreen.
- Retain the current light-theme normal player, hardware-faithful eleven-button layout, per-ROM orientation override, library/save behavior, all four display effects, audio, keyboard and multitouch support. No new settings, core changes or framework are needed.

## Context and reproduction

Current baseline: `main` at [f11fde9](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/f11fde920c4e7de962b49e8c9f82b9fb89969a08), after #145. Inspect the latest main before editing.

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): `#game` already groups the screen and eleven touch buttons. `#controls` is the separate toolbar containing `#pause`, `#reset`, sound/volume, display and fullscreen controls. The cartridge area, Help and picker are separate.
- [`web/src/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): narrow and coarse-pointer layouts currently place the toolbar after gameplay (or after feedback in landscape); `#player:fullscreen` rules retain application chrome. Replace the relevant layout rules without undoing #143's orientation/controller geometry.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): `running`, `setRunning()`, `resumeAfterDialog`, `visibilityRevision`, `readRevision`, `readROM()`, `load()`, `restart()`, `failed()`, `visibilitychange`, `pagehide`, input clearing, audio scheduling and `fullscreenchange` are the relevant lifecycle paths. Currently the hidden event sets running false and clears the Help-resume flag; there is no corresponding visible-event resume. Fullscreen currently calls `player.requestFullscreen()`.
- SNES reference at [7a039b0](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/commit/7a039b0c0aec8aceea5058a45bfc024f451885dd): [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7a039b0c0aec8aceea5058a45bfc024f451885dd/web/index.html), [web/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7a039b0c0aec8aceea5058a45bfc024f451885dd/web/style.css), [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/7a039b0c0aec8aceea5058a45bfc024f451885dd/web/app.js). Its `#game-presentation` is the fullscreen target and it provides `#exit-fullscreen`, manages focus/inert chrome, and calls its reset action **Reset**. SNES does not currently auto-pause on visibility change; do not copy that policy, because WonderSwan should suspend in the background and resume on return.
- Related: #136 / #137 (streamlined UI), #138 / #139 (local ROM library), #140 / #141 (built-in original IPL), #142 / #143 (physical controller layout and orientation), #144 / #145 (Pages deployment).

Reproduce with the existing source-built CC0 horizontal and vertical keypad fixtures in a 375×812 touch viewport and a short landscape viewport. Observe management controls near the game controls, hide/show the page during playback, and enter fullscreen.

### A. Spatial separation and Reset terminology

- Use a compact toolbar above the gameplay area in touch/mobile layouts, including upright and short landscape phones and larger coarse-pointer screens. The picture and all eleven controls should form a coherent dedicated gameplay region. Desktop layout can keep its existing sensible arrangement if no touch adjacency issue exists.
- Keep Reset, Pause/Resume, Mute/volume, Display and Fullscreen in the normal management region. The game screen and/or meaningful noninteractive separation must keep the Pause/Reset hit targets out of the immediate gameplay thumb area. This matters especially for vertical games, where A/B and Start may be next to the top or side of the screen: check both effective game orientations and adjust spacing/alignment accordingly, not just the horizontal example. Do not place dangerous controls immediately alongside Y1, A, Start or other edge buttons in landscape.
- Keep Reset as a clearly labeled normal toolbar button, using the existing `#reset` identifier and reset behavior; no extra confirmation, hidden menu or gesture. Update visible Restart wording in README, Help, errors, accessible labels and related tests where referring to this action. Internal Rust/API names such as `restart()` may remain unchanged.
- Preserve save flushing and original IPL reboot behavior when Reset is intentionally activated. Do not add a new save-state mechanism. Also keep the model selector and cartridge switching controls spatially distinct from gameplay, since model/cartridge changes can restart play.
- Keep 44×44 CSS pixel game-button targets, no hit-area overlap, safe-area insets and touch isolation. Do not shrink controls or distort the picture to fit the toolbar. If a small screen cannot fit all content, allow sensible scrolling outside gameplay, with game screen/control visibility prioritized and all normal management/error-recovery actions reachable.
- Maintain stable geometry when Pause changes to Resume, notices appear, or a finger is held on a gameplay button; the management controls must not shift under a held gameplay pointer. Do not let an ordinary game-button drag, release, cancellation or repeated tap activate Pause/Reset.

### B. Visibility suspension and automatic resume

Represent the user's playback intent separately from the actual scheduler state (or an equivalent explicit, well-tested suspension state). Visibility changes are a temporary execution constraint, not a user Pause command.

Required state behavior:

| State before becoming hidden | While hidden | On return |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Running loaded cartridge | Suspend CPU/frame production and audio; clear input and persist progress | Automatically resume normal-speed gameplay once eligible |
| User manually paused | Stay paused | Stay paused |
| Help or another playback-blocking modal open | No hidden execution | Do not run behind a blocking modal; after dismissal restore only previously intended playback |
| Faulted/stopped or no ROM | Stay stopped | Stay stopped |
| Cartridge read/load pending | No hidden guest execution or stale load/focus | Respect the current load revision, the explicit load intent and any existing pause/modal/fault constraints; resume only an eligible successfully loaded cartridge |

- Distinguish explicit Pause/Resume from temporary visibility suspension and any existing modal suspension. Repeated hide/show events and overlapping Help/visibility events must be idempotent; they must not lose the pre-modal playing intent or resurrect a user-paused game.
- Preserve existing picker semantics: merely opening/canceling it, reselecting identical ROM bytes, or rejecting an import must not turn a deliberately paused game into a running one. Do not introduce a new pause policy for the picker unless necessary for existing input isolation. A newly accepted different ROM retains normal user-initiated autoplay intent, subject to visibility/modal readiness.
- Guard against stale asynchronous cartridge reads, reset/model changes, fault recovery, and older visibility events. Do not let pending operations resume a replaced cartridge, run before save/RTC/console restoration, steal focus from a dialog, or bypass a fault. Avoid duplicate RAF/timer/audio production loops.
- On hide, clear keyboard, pointer and touch activation state and stop emulated CPU/frame scheduling and queued audio, preserving existing progress persistence. On return, reset scheduler timestamps/debt and audio scheduling appropriately; do **not** fast-forward CPU or generate a catch-up audio burst for background elapsed time. Preserve existing RTC wall-clock synchronization semantics separately from emulated gameplay time.
- Automatic resume should not require a new click for the CPU. Resume audio through existing Web Audio lifecycle, respecting saved mute/volume and browser autoplay restrictions. If the browser requires a gesture, retain the existing Enable audio recovery rather than treating audio unlock failure as a gameplay failure.
- Handle `pagehide` and `pageshow`/back-forward cache restoration consistently with visibility events, where applicable. Persist on departure, avoid execution after unload, and do not unexpectedly resume a manually paused page or duplicate schedulers on restoration.
- Do not use `window.blur` alone as the auto-pause trigger: losing keyboard focus while operating UI should continue to clear input as before, not silently change playback intent.
- Update Help/README to explain auto-suspend and automatic return only for games intended to be playing.

### C. Gameplay-only fullscreen

- Use the existing `#game` container or a minimal dedicated presentation wrapper as the actual Fullscreen API target. Move/update relevant orientation attributes and CSS selectors as necessary so the full-screen presentation uses the same effective per-ROM orientation as windowed play. Do not emulate fullscreen by expanding the entire page or leave a second duplicate game/controller instance.
- In fullscreen, show only the game image with correct aspect ratio/effect, the same eleven virtual input controls on touch/mobile devices, and one unobtrusive **Exit fullscreen** button where touch users need it. Hide unrelated chrome by keeping it outside the fullscreen subtree and prevent it from participating in focus/assistive-technology navigation while fullscreen is active.
- Place the touch exit control away from the gameplay thumb areas; its hit target must be accessible and not cover the picture or another button. Desktop keyboard users can use Escape/browser-native exit; provide sensible accessible exit/focus behavior without permanently cluttering the normal screen. No Pause or Reset controls in fullscreen.
- Use the available safe-area-adjusted width/height to give the picture as much room as reasonably possible. Maintain horizontal Y-above-X / diagonal A-B and vertical Y-left/X-right / rotated direction identities from #143. Phone rotation may change responsive sizing but never change the effective orientation or input bits. Do not stretch the picture, clip game buttons or make vertical games unnecessarily tiny. Preserve existing supported scale/pixel alignment and display effects.
- Entering/leaving fullscreen, including browser Escape/native exit, must not restart the cartridge, change playback intent, lose save data or change orientation preferences. Clear held input when layout changes. Correctly restore focus to the canvas or the initiating control for keyboard accessibility, including when exit is activated by touch. Do not steal focus from an active modal or scroll the normal layout unexpectedly.
- Recalculate presentation dimensions/effect sizing on fullscreen entry/exit and viewport resize. A paused frame must redraw at the new size without executing the game. Maintain existing audio recovery behavior and ensure meaningful error/recovery information is reachable after exiting fullscreen.
- Where Fullscreen API is unavailable or denied, show concise existing-style feedback and keep ordinary gameplay usable. Do not force device orientation or require a particular mobile browser.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Update the normal touch layouts so player-management controls appear above and are clearly separated from gameplay. Test horizontal and vertical effective game orientations in portrait 375×812, short landscape 812×375 and constrained 320×568 (or equivalent) touch viewports. Use DOM geometry/hit-target checks to verify Pause/Reset are not adjacent to or overlapping game input hit regions, including upper/right-side buttons for vertical play; ensure all eleven controls remain reachable and at least 44×44 CSS pixels. Capture representative screenshots and document any constrained scrolling. Keep toolbar/error recovery/cartridge controls reachable.
- [ ] Rename the user-visible Restart action to Reset. Verify a single intentional click/keyboard activation resets the guest using the existing original-IPL path and preserves completed save data. No confirmation/menu/extra gesture. Test representative touch presses, releases, drags/cancellation and repeated taps near the edges of the controller; no unintended Reset or Pause, guest reboot, or stuck input.
- [ ] Add focused real-Wasm browser regressions for visibility lifecycle. Prove actual guest frame/CPU progress stops while hidden and resumes automatically when shown if previously playing; a manually paused game remains paused. Verify no input remains held, no duplicate scheduler, no elapsed-time catch-up, and correct audio pause/resume behavior using the existing instrumentation or equivalent. Exercise repeated hide/show and relevant Help/modal, pending load/revision, faulted and unloaded cases. Test visibility and page lifecycle events realistically where possible; label any simulated event tests and do not claim a physical tab switch was tested if not.
- [ ] Fullscreen API selects the dedicated gameplay container, not `#player`. In touch fullscreen verify the picture, eleven correctly arranged buttons and Exit fullscreen; no normal toolbar/header/cartridge/console/settings controls or off-screen focus traps. On desktop verify game-focused fullscreen and keyboard/native exit. Check both game orientations in portrait and landscape viewports, aspect ratio/corner markers, active display effect, safe areas, and non-overlapping exit/game hit targets. Test actual fullscreen entry/exit where supported and unavailable/rejected API recovery. Verify focus/input, paused redraw, continued gameplay and unchanged ROM/setting/save identity across fullscreen transitions.
- [ ] Preserve existing ROM picker and per-ROM orientation behavior, raw SHA-256 identities, SRAM/EEPROM/RTC persistence, eleven physical input masks, combined keyboard/multitouch, visibility save flushing, sound/mute/volume and all display modes. Reuse the original CC0 keypad/save fixtures and extend existing browser checks; no commercial ROM, proprietary BIOS, physical phone, or subjective human sign-off is required.
- [ ] Update README and Help for Reset, automatic resume, and gameplay-only fullscreen. Run the applicable production-preview gates in `web`: `npm ci`, `npm run build:wasm` if needed to obtain current Wasm, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat`, plus `git diff --check`. Reuse builds and apply the repository's test/CI performance principles. Core and fixture source checks are required only if those sources or relevant core behavior change. Record actual browser versions, test results, screenshots and limitations; do not relax existing assertions merely to pass.

## Optional validation

Exercise mobile WebKit, physical smartphones and browser back-forward cache/real background-tab behavior if available. Report what was actually tested. These are supplemental, not blockers.

## Required post-merge verification

After implementation and mandatory pre-merge checks pass, merge and close this Issue according to the repository lifecycle. Verify the normal GitHub Pages deployment for the merge revision, record the workflow URL/revision, and exercise the published player using original CC0 fixtures: normal mobile gameplay with separated Pause/Reset, automatic resume after a visibility interruption versus manual pause, gameplay-only fullscreen and exit in both game orientations. Record actual production results and limitations, including unavailable fullscreen/visibility tests if applicable. Track confirmed production defects in a linked follow-up rather than reopening solely for pending deployment verification.
